description: The Projector Output window (FR-102), granted NOTHING — and the file exists so that emptiness is a statement someone wrote rather than an omission nobody noticed (SEC-01, ADR-0041). An empty permissions list is the entire content: no app-defined command, and not core:event:default either. PRD 6.3 puts this window's whole lifecycle in the Rust Display Service and PRD 6.5 has the slide-advance hot path broadcast TO it, so what it needs is to receive, not to call; on the day it must listen for events itself, core:event:default is added here by the item that needs it and by nothing else. Before SEC-01 this file could not have helped: "windows" scoping binds ACL-gated commands only, and app-defined commands were not ACL-gated at all, so the output window could invoke list_monitors — and every command added after it — with no trace in any manifest (ADR-0041). src-tauri/permissions/ now exists, so an app-defined command can reach this window OVER IPC only through a capability that names it, and none does. At least three things this file does not and cannot cover, named here so its emptiness is not read as a wider boundary than it is. The count is left open deliberately: closed enumerations have been wrong three times in this repository, and the missing item was always the one nobody had looked for. First, plugin:__TAURI_CHANNEL__|fetch is exempt from the ACL inside tauri's own condition (webview/mod.rs:1823-1826), so it is callable from here whatever this file says; the cost is zero while the application creates no Channel, and the first item that creates one owns it. Second, ADR-0042: output.html and index.html share an origin, so script running in this window can reach the Control Panel document through BroadcastChannel, localStorage or a MessageChannel without an invoke and without touching the ACL at all. Third, top-level navigation. Until SEC-02 this window had no navigation guard at all, and the mechanism recorded here was itself wrong: tauri sets pending.navigation_handler unconditionally (manager/webview.rs:580) and what was None is the INNER handler (ADR-0042, correction of 2026-08-28). Navigation away from this bundle is now refused unless the URL matches an origin this build actually serves, decided in src-tauri/src/services/navigation.rs from the per-window configuration rather than from a hardcoded host, so the ACL saying nothing about how a document got into a window is no longer the whole story. That guard is not the ACL and does not extend it, and three paths still fail OPEN, all named in that module: tauri's own wrapper answers true while the label is still absent from webviews_lock(), so the FIRST navigation of every window is never offered to the guard; tauri-runtime-wry permits any URI string its Url::parse rejects (.unwrap_or(true)); and window.open raises NewWindowRequested, which wry happens to drop on its own rather than by anything written here. CSP still governs none of it - no directive covers top-level navigation, navigate-to was never implemented in Chromium and form-action 'none' closes only form submission - so that sentence was true before SEC-02 and stays true after it. And navigation is not the only way out of this window: neither window sets a download handler, so a programmatic anchor with the download attribute writes a file to disk from a window this file declares granted NOTHING. That surface belongs to FR-105 (SEC-02 audit, W5), and the word NOTHING above must not be read as covering it. None of the three is exploitable today — the frontend's only invoke() is in src/main/App.vue and it relays nothing — but a Control Panel that ever acts on a same-origin message hands this window the reach this file was written to withhold. src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs states both in full. Do not give any capability that grants an app-defined command a glob such as "windows": ["*"], and do not name "output" in one: scripts/check-command-inventory.js rejects both, because a glob is precisely how this window would get its reach back without anyone reading a diff that says so. NFR-13, NFR-14.
